title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2 close: Milevis and Orange preach justifying/converting inspiration not given promiscuously to all — Synod of African exiles in Sardinia
pass_a_gloss: But let us pass unto the Councils, of which one may generally affirm that Such a Grace of Christ is preached in them as experience itself cries out is not given promiscuously unto all. Milevis declares that The grace of God given unto us through Jesus Christ is the grace of justification, can. 3, 4, and 5. But that this (whatever be established concerning exciting and illuminating grace) is not common unto all, no one doubts. The same is the sentence of Orange, which teaches that this grace of which we now inquire is the inspiration of the Holy Spirit correcting our will from unbelief unto faith, from impiety unto piety, Can. 5. But that such and so efficacious an inspiration is given unto some, not given unto others, is so plain that to deny it is not ignorance only but folly. Finally we have an excellent and most express testimony in the Synodical Epistle of the Bishops exiled in Sardinia. Thus therefore they; He does not think worthily of grace, whosoever thinks it is given unto all men. A little after they show what grace they mean, namely that which works in a man both to will and to do. They go on, and explain further in whom God’s grace works this; This, they say, it works in his own, that they may work their own salvation. But who at length are those whom God acknowledges as his own? Presently it follows; All the predestinated themselves are those whom God wills to be made safe. From all which it follows that There are certain ones unto whom this grace efficacious unto salvation was never either given or destined.
pass_b_english: Turn to the councils: in them such a Grace of Christ is preached as experience itself cries is not given promiscuously to all. Milevis declares (can. 3–5) that the grace of God given through Jesus Christ is the grace of justification—and no one doubts that this (whatever is said of exciting and illuminating grace) is not common to all. Orange teaches the same (can. 5): the grace now in question is the Holy Spirit’s inspiration correcting our will from unbelief to faith, from impiety to piety. That such efficacious inspiration is given to some and not others is so plain that to deny it is folly, not mere ignorance. Best and most express is the Synodical Letter of the bishops exiled in Sardinia: He does not think worthily of grace who thinks it is given to all men. A little later they name the grace they mean—the one that works in a man both to will and to do—and add: This it works in his own, that they may work their salvation. Who are those God owns? Presently: All the predestined themselves are those God wills to be saved. So some never had this grace efficacious to salvation given or destined to them.
source_text: Verum ad Concilia transeamus, de quibus illud generatim affirmare licet, Gratiam Christi talem in illis praedicari, qualem omnibus non dari promiscue clamat ipsa experientia. Milevitanum, Gratiam Dei per Jesum Christum nobis donatam, gratiam justificationis esse, declarat, can. 3, 4, et 5. Hanc autem (quicquid de excitante et illuminante gratia statuatur) non esse omnium communem nemo dubitat. Eadem est sententia Arausicani, quod docet hanc gratiam de qua nunc quaeritur, esse inspirationem Spiritus sancti corrigentem voluntatem nostram ab infidelitate ad fidem, ab impietate ad pietatem, Can. 5. Talem autem ac tam efficacem inspirationem aliquibus dari, aliquibus non dari, adeo manifestum est, ut non inscitiae solum, sed stultitiae sit illud negare. Denique, habemus optimum et maxime expressum testimonium in Epistola Synodica Episcoporum in Sardinia exsulantium. Sic igitur illi; De gratia non digne sentit, quisquis eam putat omnibus hominibus dari. Paulo post ostendunt quam gratiam intelligunt, nempe eam quae in homine operatur et velle et facere. Pergunt, atque explicant insuper in quibus Dei gratia hoc operatur; Hoc, inquiunt, operatur in suis, ut suam salutem operentur. Sed quinam tandem sunt illi quos Deus pro suis agnoscit? Mox sequitur; Omnes praedestinati ipsi sunt quos Deus vult salvos fieri. Ex quibus omnibus consequitur, Esse aliquos quibus nec data nec destinata unquam fuit haec gratia efficax ad salutem.
